docs.text: BagaPie BagaPie is a free, open-source toolbox for architecture and environment work in Blender. It gathers about fifty tools, most of them built on Geometry Nodes: scattering, ivy, arrays, walls, stairs, windows, booleans, groups and more. BagaPie 11 · Blender extension · GPL-3.0-or-later This edition follows BagaPie 11.0.11. Its extension manifest requires Blender 5.0 or newer . The BagaPie 11 tutorials apply to every BagaPie 11 build from Blender 4.2 onward; menus may differ slightly on older builds. Select assets, then the surface, press J and choose Scatter. In short Select what the tool needs: nothing, one object, or several objects with a target selected last. Press J in Object Mode, or D in Edit Mode, and pick a tool. Adjust the result in the BagaPie tab of the 3D Viewport sidebar ( N ). Most tools stay parametric: you can change them at any time from the BagaPie panel. Edit Mode tools are applied as soon as you leave their operator panel, except Windows and Doors. docs.text: Asset libraries BagaPie uses two kinds of asset libraries. Both are set up from Preferences > Assets . BagaPie Parametric Library (free, CC0) Click Setup BagaPie's Parametric Library CC-0 . BagaPie adds a library named BagaPie Modifier to the Asset Browser, filled with BagaPie presets. This library also contains the Geometry Nodes tools of the Edit Mode pie . After the first setup, restart Blender : the tools are only available after a restart. If the Edit Mode pie shows Tool File missing ! after an update, click Update BagaPie Parametric Library , then restart Blender. BagaPie Assets (optional, paid) BagaPie Assets is an asset library sold separately on SuperHive and Gumroad. It funds the development of BagaPie. It includes vegetation, rocks and other assets, and around forty scatter presets for GeoPack. BagaPie Assets is optional: every BagaPie tool works the same way with your own assets. Install the packs Packs are .baga files. In Preferences > Assets , click Set BagaPie Assets Packs Storage Location and choose a folder. Click Install BagaPie Asset Pack (.baga files) and select a pack. Repeat for each pack. Packs are installed one by one, and each installation can take several seconds. The preferences list the packs (Lite, Essential and full volumes) and show the installed ones in green. Edit Library Location changes the storage folder; the folder icon opens it. After updating BagaPie, if no packs are found, use Set library location to point BagaPie to the folder where your packs are already installed. Material panels Some BagaPie Assets materials (grass, plants, rocks, trees, stumps) have their own settings in the BagaPie panel when the asset is selected: tint, brightness, saturation and their random variations, ambient occlusion, translucency, specular, roughness, and a Season slider for vegetation. Season values above 0.9 add transparency, which can increase render time. Lower Season or Random Season if renders slow down.

docs.text: Group BagaPie groups put objects inside a common bounding box. They make large scenes easier to manage, work in animation, and can be turned into instances to lighten a scene. Create a group Select the objects, press J and choose Create Group , or press Ctrl + G . Select the objects and choose Create Group. A bounding box is created and the group tools appear in the panel. BagaPie creates a bounding box. Its content is no longer selectable: select the box to move the whole group. Groups can contain other groups. Group shortcut If the panel shows Add Group Shortcut , click it: Ctrl + G then creates groups, and gives quick access to the group tools when a group is selected. Save your preferences, or the shortcut is reset at the next start. Group tools Select the bounding box to display the group tools in the BagaPie panel. Button Action Make Content Selectable / Make Content Unselectable Unlock or lock the selection of the group content. All also applies to groups inside the group Group to Instance Replace the group with an instance (see below) Isolate / Unisolate Edit the group alone, then come back Ungroup Remove the group, keep the objects Delete Group (ALL) Delete the group and its content Add / Remove (Group Content) Add the selected objects to the group, or remove them Link Obj to Group Coll Only Unlink the group objects from every other collection Move Instance Group Move the group source without moving its instances Double Clic Edit Turn double click editing on (beta) Link Obj to Group Coll Only removes the objects from all collections except the group collection. If these objects are needed in other collections, do not use it. Add and remove content Add: select the objects to add, then the group (last), and click Add . Remove: make the content selectable, select the objects, and click Remove . Double click edit (beta) With Double Clic Edit on, double click a group bounding box or a group instance to isolate it for editing. Double click in empty space, or click Exit Editing , to come back. Press Esc to turn double click editing off. Groups and instances Group to Instance replaces the group with an empty that instances the group collection. The original group is moved to the world origin. Changes made to the group are repeated on every instance. Think of the empty as the world origin of the group: objects are placed relative to it. To move the source group without affecting its instances, use Move Instance Group . Use it only when instances of the group exist. Select an instance and click Edit Instance Group , or double click it, to edit the group. Duplicate instances freely to repeat elements in a scene. To Instance , in the Manage section of the J pie, creates the group and the instance in one step. Duplicate Shortcut Action Alt + J Duplicate the group and its content Alt + N Linked duplicate: meshes stay linked, like Alt + D compared to Shift + D

Scatter presets with GeoPack Save complete scatter setups as presets. Export and share them as .geopack files; assets are packed automatically. Previews are generated from the current view. Asset Browser panel Displays all scatter layers. One-click scatter from the selected assets. Per-asset controls: proxy, bounds, select, remove. Easy layer renaming. Group system rewritten Groups inside groups. To Instance in one click; switch between group and instances. Dynamic bounding box. Ctrl + G to create a group, double click to edit (beta). 20 new tools Face to Grid, Face to Paving, Face to Perforated Grid, Face to Plank. Window Modern, Window Classic, Door Simple, Door Double. Cable Creator, Bool Through, Tessellate, Insert Circle. Array Along Shape, Bolt Corner. Scatter improvements Improved preview generator. Snap Asset uses the object offset, Bevel Weight and Vertex Crease. UI fixes in Scatter Paint and a simpler Scatter panel. Plus many bug fixes and UI improvements.

docs.text: Troubleshooting Everything disappears when I apply a modifier Apply BagaPie modifiers from the BagaPie panel ( N ): click ✓ in the modifier stack. BagaPie applies all the modifiers that belong together. Modifiers have an order: apply the ones above yours first. My scatter or ivy is not stable during an animation Scatter and ivy positions are computed from the surface area of the target. If the object is animated or deformed, its area changes, and so does the distribution. There is currently no solution for this in BagaPie. My scatter or ivy is different in the render Check that the surface does not change at render time, for example a different Subdivision level for the render. Check % Viewport Display : the viewport can show fewer instances than the render. The pie menu does not open J works in Object Mode, D in Edit Mode on a mesh with something selected, V in Object Mode. Check that your BagaPie version is compatible with your Blender version. See Installation . Check the shortcuts in Preferences > Preferences > Menu Shortcuts . The Edit Mode pie shows "SETUP TOOL !" or "Restart Blender" Click SETUP TOOL ! , then restart Blender. This is needed once after installing or updating. See Asset libraries . A tool is grayed out The selection does not match the tool. Check what to select in Object Mode Pie , or in Preferences > Pie Menu Tools . For targets, select the target last . The Asset Browser button does nothing or is grayed out An Asset Browser must be open, with assets selected. Select assets in a specific library, not in All . Only Object and Collection assets are imported. The active object in the viewport must be a mesh. "Save in GeoPack" is grayed out Open Preferences > GeoPack and set the packs location if asked. Select your object (mesh or curve). In the modifier stack, click the Geometry Nodes modifier to save: it gets a blue outline. Windows: shutters are missing Shutters only work on quad faces; they are disabled on n-gons. If a few shutters fail, tweak Min Height . See Windows & Doors . The boolean of a window or door does not cut the whole wall The default is set for a 20 cm wall. Increase the wall thickness in the operator panel, or Boolean Thickness in the BagaPie panel. The Group shortcut is lost after restarting Blender Click Add Group Shortcut , then save your preferences. Still stuck? Ask on Discord . Include your Blender and BagaPie versions, and a screenshot of the BagaPie panel if possible.

docs.text: Mesh tools All tools on this page are applied: adjust them in the operator panel (bottom left) before clicking elsewhere. Cable Creator Creates cables from selected edges . Select edges. Press D and choose Cable Creator . The main setting is the deformation: increase its intensity and adjust the frequency . A higher frequency gives fewer deformations along the cable, a lower one a more chaotic cable. Change the seed for variations. The cable deforms according to the surface. Bool Through Cuts a hole through the mesh from the selected faces. Select the faces. Press D and choose Bool Through . The faces are projected onto the opposite side of the mesh, along their average normal. It also works on complex shapes, such as beveled faces. If the boolean looks unfinished, increase the offset . Tessellate Replaces faces with an object of your choice. Select the faces (quads only). Press D and choose Tessellate . In the operator panel, pick the mesh to use. The object's origin determines where it is placed relative to each face. Insert Circle Inserts a circle into any face: triangle, quad or n-gon. Settings: rotation, number of sides, offset and radius. The radius is not set automatically; adjust it for small or large scales. Array Along Shape Repeats part of a mesh along the closest surface of the same object, and deforms it. Join the element to repeat and the surface into one object. In Edit Mode, select only the faces to repeat. Press D and choose Array Along Shape . Enable Snap Deform to deform the repeated mesh along the surface. On curved surfaces, increase the precision. Unlock the axes to rotate the array axis. A parametric version, working with separate objects, is in the Object Mode pie . Bolt Corner Adds bolts or screws in the corners of the selected faces. Settings: Offset to move them toward the face center, the bolt or screw type, and Custom Object to use your own asset.

docs.text: Windows & Doors Windows and doors are cut into a wall from selected faces. Unlike the other Edit Mode tools, they stay parametric . Add windows or doors In Edit Mode, select one or more faces of the wall. Quads work best; n-gons are supported. Press D and choose Window Modern , Window Classic , Door Simple or Door Double . In the operator panel (bottom left), set the wall thickness and the boolean solver ( Exact or Fast ). Select faces on the wall, press D and choose a window. The wall is cut and the windows are created. The selected faces are copied to a new window (or door) object. Blender leaves Edit Mode on the wall. You get three objects: the wall, the window object and a hidden boolean object, which you do not need to edit. Edit after creation Select the window object and enter Edit Mode: each face is a window. Move or scale a face to move or resize its window; the wall topology does not change. Use loop cuts ( Ctrl + R ) on a window face to split it. Each frame adapts to its new size. All settings are in the BagaPie panel, with a Material section at the bottom. docs.text: GeoPack: install and use packs GeoPack lets you install, create and share custom tools for BagaPie. A pack is a set of Geometry Nodes modifiers, with their usage rules, icons, and optionally an asset library and scatter presets. Packs are shared as .geopack files. Think of a pack as a small add-on built with Geometry Nodes, without code. Packs you create are yours: you can export, share or sell them, and anyone with BagaPie can install them. Set the pack location The first time, choose where packs are stored on your computer. Open Edit > Preferences > Add-ons > BagaPie and expand GeoPack . Click Set packs location and pick a folder. Packs already in that folder are detected and listed. You can move packs to another folder later: open Storage , set the new path, and click Move all packs to new location . Install a pack In Preferences > GeoPack , click Install Pack . Select the .geopack file and confirm. If the pack includes assets, BagaPie creates an asset library for it automatically. A free Demo Pack ( Demo Pack.geopack ) comes with the BagaPie download on SuperHive and Gumroad. Pack details Expand a pack in the preferences to see: Info: description, authors, version, license, minimum Blender version, link. Modifier: the tools of the pack, each with an icon, information and how this modifier will work : what to select and what happens. Read it before using a tool. Assets: the pack's asset library and its files. The eye icons hide a pack, or one of its modifiers, from the pie menu. Use a pack In Object Mode, press V . The GeoPack pie menu lists the installed packs. Pick a pack, then a tool. Grayed-out tools mean the selection does not match what the tool needs. If the pack author used Node to Panel , the tool settings appear in the BagaPie panel. If no pack is installed, the pie menu tells you to set a location or install a pack. docs.text: Create a pack You can turn any Geometry Nodes modifier into a GeoPack tool, then share the pack as a .geopack file. 1. Create the pack In Preferences > GeoPack , set the packs location if needed. Click Create New Pack and fill in: Pack Name , Pack Author(s) , Description , Pack Version , Pack URL Oldest Blender Version Compatible Pack License : Royalty Free, CC0, CC-BY, GPL or MIT Pack Location Click Create ! . 2. Add a modifier to the pack In the 3D Viewport, select the object (mesh or curve) that has your Geometry Nodes modifier. In the modifier stack, click the modifier to save so it becomes active (blue outline). Press J and choose New GeoPack Modifier (About section). With Node to Panel , the BagaPie panel also has a Save as GeoPack Modifier button. In the dialog, choose the pack ( Add to pack ), fill in the information and define how the tool is set up (see below). Click OK . The tool now appears in the GeoPack pie menu ( V ). The modifier name comes from its node tree name, without the BP_ prefix if there is one. If the name is already used, BagaPie asks you to rename the node tree, or to Override the existing modifier. Information Modifier name , Author(s) , Description , Modifier Version , Minimal Blender version , Contact , URL , NodeTree License . Usage: how the tool is set up This defines what the user must select and what happens when they click the tool. Active Object Must Be Option Behavior Mesh , Curve , Mesh or Curve The tool is grayed out unless the active object has this type. The modifier is added to it None - Create new object Ignores the selection and creates a new object, mesh or curve Depending on the choice, extra options appear: New mesh: Switch to Edit Mode and enable Add Cube tool . New curve: Switch to draw curve mode , with Curve Mode (2D / 3D) and Curve Projection (Cursor / Surface). Existing mesh: Switch to Weight Paint (a new vertex group is created and assigned to an attribute input of your modifier), or Add Hair Curves . Add Curve and switch to draw mode: a new curve is created and plugged into an object input of the modifier. Use Selection Uses the other selected objects. Choose which object types are accepted ( Mesh , Curve , Camera , Empty , Text , Volume , Light ), the Collection Name and the Collection Input of the modifier that receives them. Allow asset browser selection adds an Asset Browser button to the tool. The dialog summarizes the result under How your modifier will work . The same summary is shown to users in the pack details. 3. Icons Each modifier can have an icon in the pie menu. In the pack details, use Add Icon , the remove button, or the refresh button. Icon size in the pie menu is set by GeoPack Icon Scale in the preferences. 4. Assets A pack can include its own asset library: In the pack details, open Assets and click Create Asset Library . Click Add blend file to Pack's Assets Library to add .blend files. The library is created automatically for users who install the pack. 5. Edit, export, delete Edit: the pencil icons edit the pack information or a modifier. Export: the export icon saves the pack as a .geopack file to share. Delete: deletes the pack or a modifier. Deleting a pack also deletes all assets linked to it, and cannot be undone. Keep a copy. Save your preferences after creating or moving packs.

docs.text: Node to Panel Node to Panel turns the inputs of your own Geometry Nodes modifiers into a clean interface in the BagaPie panel. You organize inputs with prefixes. It is useful for complex node trees and for GeoPack tools, but works without GeoPack too. Display a modifier Add BP_ at the beginning of the node tree name (not the modifier name). The modifier then appears in the BagaPie panel of the object. In GeoPack, the tool is named after the node tree, without BP_ . Prefixes Add prefixes to the input names. A prefix ends with _ , followed by the displayed name. Prefixes can also be written in the input description: right-click an input in the node group interface and use the BagaPie Node to Panel menu to add them. Prefix Displays V_ A value (any input type) L_ A label P_ A button (boolean input) P1_ … P9_ A button with an identifier from 0 to 9, which can show or hide other inputs 1V_ … An input controlled by button 1 (put the identifier first) C_ The curve of a Float Curve or Color Ramp node: the input name must match the node name or label S_ A separator; add the size after it URL_ A button that opens a link. Use a String input and put the URL in its default value B_ / B Create a new box / add to the previous box R_ / R Create a new row / add to the previous row 2_ (any integer) Scale the input or button Prefixes combine. Examples: Input name Result B_L_MyLabelName A new box with a label P_MyButtonName A switch button R_V_MyValueName A , then RV_MyValueName B Two values on one row P1_Hit me ! , 1V_MyValueName_A , 1V_MyValueName_B A button that shows or hides two values Boxes and rows can be nested. Tips Inputs are displayed in order, from top to bottom. Float Curve and Color Ramp nodes appear at the position of their input, but their relative order is not controllable. If several nodes share the same name or label, they are all displayed. Rename a node with F2 . Hide inputs that are only used for layout (labels, separators) in the modifier. Shader node groups using the same prefixes are displayed too, under the object's materials. At the bottom of the panel, Save as GeoPack Modifier adds the modifier to a pack, with its interface. See Create a pack . The prefix list is also in Preferences > Nodes to Panel , with examples.

docs.text: Scatter presets A complete scatter setup can be saved in a GeoPack and reused in one click, in any file. Applying a preset replaces the current scatter of the surface. Save a preset Set up the scatter on a surface. See Scattering . Make sure you have a pack to save it in. See Create a pack . Frame the surface in the 3D view: the preview is rendered from the current view. At the bottom of the scatter settings, open Save in GeoPack : Generate Preview Icon (on by default) Lighting: Use Current World to light the preview with your world Click Save Scatter in GeoPack , choose the pack, and name the preset (required). Keep Preview Generation checked. The other information is optional and can be edited later. In Usage , keep Active Object set to Mesh , the default, and click OK . Saving takes a few seconds: BagaPie renders the preview and copies the assets into the pack. What is saved All scatter layers of the surface. The assets, stored inside the pack. A preview, generated from the current view and the active object. Camera culling, effectors and weight paint are not saved: they belong to the scene, not to the scatter system. Preview settings (resolution, samples, exposure, sun, focal length) are in Preferences > Preferences > GeoPack Scatter Icon Generator Settings . Use a preset Select a surface, press V , choose the pack, then the preset. If the surface already has a scatter, BagaPie warns you that the new scatter will replace it, and that its camera culling and effectors will be lost. Share The preset is a modifier of the pack: you can change its preview or information in Preferences > GeoPack . Export the pack as a .geopack file to share it. The paid BagaPie Assets library includes around forty scatter presets.

docs.text: Installation Install from Blender (recommended) BagaPie is published on the Blender Extensions platform. Installing it from there gives you one-click updates. Open Edit > Preferences > Get Extensions . Search for BagaPie . Click Install . Save your preferences if they are not saved automatically. BagaPie is also distributed on SuperHive, Gumroad and BlenderKit. It is the same add-on on every platform, but only the Extensions platform version updates from inside Blender. Install from a ZIP file If you downloaded the ZIP: Drag the ZIP from your file browser into an open Blender window and confirm, or Use Edit > Preferences > Get Extensions > menu (˅) > Install from Disk… and select the ZIP. Do not unzip the file. Blender installs it directly from the archive. Update Extensions platform: open Edit > Preferences > Get Extensions and click Update next to BagaPie. ZIP install: uninstall the previous BagaPie, restart Blender, then install the new ZIP. First-time setup These steps are optional, but recommended. Parametric Library. In the BagaPie preferences, open Assets and click Setup BagaPie's Parametric Library CC-0 . This adds a BagaPie Modifier library to the Asset Browser. The Edit Mode pie menu ( D ) needs it, then a Blender restart. See Asset libraries . Group shortcut. If BagaPie offers Add Group Shortcut (in the panel, the pie menu or the preferences), click it to use Ctrl + G for BagaPie groups, then save your preferences. See Group . GeoPack location. Before installing a GeoPack, choose a folder for your packs in Preferences > GeoPack . See GeoPack . Which version for which Blender? docs.text: How BagaPie works Select, press a key, pick a tool BagaPie tools are launched from pie menus in the 3D Viewport. Select the objects the tool needs. When a tool uses a target (a surface, a curve), select the target last so it becomes the active object. Press J (Object Mode) or D (Edit Mode). Click a tool. Grayed-out buttons mean the current selection does not match what the tool needs. The selection depends on the tool: Tool needs Examples Nothing Stair Spiral, Beam, Beam Wire: a new object is created at the 3D cursor One object Wall (mesh edges), Displace, Line Array, Proxy Objects + a target selected last Scatter, Snap Asset, Array Along Shape, Curve Deform A curve, or nothing Fence, Handrail: without a curve, BagaPie creates one and switches to Draw mode Faces or edges in Edit Mode Windows, Doors, Bool Through, Cable Creator The full list is in Object Mode Pie and Edit Mode Pie . It is also available in Preferences > Pie Menu Tools , with what each tool expects. The BagaPie panel Open the 3D Viewport sidebar with N and select the BagaPie tab. Press Ctrl + Alt + J to open the same panel as a pop-up. At the top, the modifier stack lists the BagaPie modifiers of the active object. Select one to display its settings below. Each line offers, depending on the modifier: Icon Action ✓ Apply : convert the modifier result to real geometry. Use this button rather than Blender's Apply: BagaPie applies all the modifiers that belong together. − Remove the BagaPie modifier and its helper objects Monitor / camera Show or hide in the viewport / in renders Scatter layers, effectors and camera culling have extra icons in this list; see Scattering . When a group is selected, the panel shows the group tools instead. Geometry Nodes modifiers prepared with Node to Panel are also displayed there. The panel ends with links to the tutorial playlist and the documentation. Parametric and applied tools Object Mode tools add modifiers. Their settings stay editable in the BagaPie panel until you apply or remove them. Edit Mode tools run once on the selected faces or edges. You can tweak them in Blender's operator panel (bottom left) until you click elsewhere; then the result is permanent. Windows and Doors are the exception: they stay parametric. Collections created by BagaPie BagaPie stores helper objects in a BagaPie collection, with sub-collections such as BagaPie_Scatter , BagaPie_Boolean or BagaPie_Assets . Avoid deleting them manually while the related modifiers are still in use; use the remove button in the BagaPie panel instead. Assets from the Asset Browser Several tools have an Asset Browser button next to them (Scatter, Scatter Paint, Snap Asset, Draw array). It imports the assets selected in an open Asset Browser and runs the tool with them. Open an Asset Browser area and select one or more Object or Collection assets. Browse a specific library. The All library is not supported. In the viewport, select the target mesh, then click the Asset Browser button in the pie menu. Imported assets are placed in the BagaPie_Assets collection.

docs.text: Array The Array section repeats objects along a line, a grid, a circle, a curve, a drawn stroke or a surface. Unlike Blender's Array modifier, BagaPie arrays include random position, rotation and scale. Line, Grid and Circle Select one object (mesh or curve), press J and choose Line , Grid or Circle . Arrays support one object at a time; repeat the operation for each object. Type Settings Line Count, Constant Offset, Relative Offset Grid Count X / Y, Constant Offset X / Y, Relative Offset X / Y, Midlevel X / Y Circle Count or Distance mode, Constant Distance, Count, Circle Resolution, Radius, Ring Count, Ring Offset, Ring Offset Z, Rotation, Align to Center All three have a Random section: Position, Rotation, Scale and Seed. Circle array: raise the Radius and the Circle Resolution, switch between Count and Distance, add rings. For a circle, a low Circle Resolution gives a polygonal shape: increase it for a round circle. Repetition can be based on a fixed Count or on the Distance between instances. Curve Repeats an object along a curve. Select the object to repeat. Select the curve last . Press J and choose Curve . Settings: Count or Length mode, Target curve, Rotation , Scale , Random Position / Rotation / Scale , Seed , and Align to Vector with its Vector . Curve Deform Deforms objects along a curve, like Blender's Array + Curve modifiers, which it uses. Select the object(s). Select the curve last . Press J and choose Curve Deform . Settings: Axis , Use Relative Offset / Relative Offset , Use Constant Offset / Constant Offset . The default axis usually fits. This array has no random options. If BagaPie reports multi-user data, apply the rotation and scale of the objects first. Draw Draws a curve and repeats the selected objects along it. Select one or more objects. Press J and choose Draw (or Asset Browser next to it to use assets selected in the Asset Browser). Draw in the viewport. BagaPie creates a new curve, enters Edit Mode with the Draw tool, and projects the stroke on the surfaces under the cursor. Settings: Count or Length , Target , Rotation , Position , Align to Curve , Scale Min / Max , random Position / Rotation and Seed . Array Along Shape Repeats objects along the shape of a surface, following it by proximity. Select the object(s) to repeat. Select the surface to follow last . Press J and choose Array Along Shape . Setting Effect Count Number of instances Precision / Distance Accuracy of the spacing between instances Position, Rotation X / Y / Normal, Scale Min / Max, Seed Randomization Orientation Angle , Smooth Rotation Orientation of the instances Lock Axis X / Y / Z By default the array is locked to one axis. Unlock axes for a freer result Target The surface followed The array can fail on sharp edges (over about 70°). Add a Bevel modifier to the surface to round them. An Edit Mode version that also deforms the repeated mesh is in the Edit Mode pie . Remove Use Remove (−) in the modifier stack.

docs.text: Effectors Effectors are extra masks for a scatter layer. They appear in the pie menu only when the active object has a BagaPie scatter; otherwise the section shows No Scatter available . Both effectors apply to one layer : select that layer in the modifier stack first. With several layers, repeat the operation for each layer. Point Effector Removes instances around objects, for example to keep rocks away from a house. In the BagaPie panel, select the scatter layer. Select the effector object(s), then the scattered surface last . Press J and choose Point Effector . Setting Effect Effector Collection The objects used as effectors Distance Min / Max Distance range of the effect. Keep both close for a sharp edge. If Min is larger than Max, the mask is inverted Density Strength of the effect Camera Culling Removes instances outside the camera view, to lighten heavy scenes. In the BagaPie panel, select the scatter layer. Select the camera (or an empty), then the scattered surface last . Press J and choose Camera Culling . Setting Effect Camera The camera used X Ratio / Y Ratio Widen the kept area. Increase them if instances disappear at the frame edges Offset Extra margin Once a camera culling exists, the Camera Culling button in the layer tools, and the camera icon in the modifier stack, assign it to other layers. Culling resolution depends on the surface resolution. Subdivide the surface if needed.

docs.text: Ivy The Ivy tool grows procedural ivy on one or more target meshes. Add ivy Place the 3D cursor where the ivy should start ( Shift + right click ). Select the target mesh(es). Press J and choose Ivy . Select the target, J > Ivy. Move the sphere empty to move the ivy source. BagaPie creates a sphere empty named Ivy_Parent at the 3D cursor. It is the ivy source: move it to move the ivy. The ivy grows toward the nearest target surface. Targets Add a target: select the new object, then the ivy, and click Add under Target . Remove a target: select the object, then the ivy, and click Remove . More sources To add another ivy that shares the same targets and settings, place the 3D cursor, select the ivy and click Add Ivy to 3D Cursor . Added parts can be deleted with Delete this part of ivy when their source is selected. The original part can only be removed with the modifier. Settings Ivy Setting Effect Spiral / Grid Project Generation system: a spiral guide projected on the targets, or a projected grid View Guide Show the guide shape, to understand how the ivy is projected Radius Size of the guide Height / Loop Spiral mode only: height and number of loops of the spiral Gravity , Scale , Resolution Shape and detail of the ivy Density / Decimate Amount of leaves, and simplification Random Random Position , Emission Area , Surface Offset , Scale and Ivy Random Position add variation to the growth and to the leaves. Collections Target , Asset and Emitter are the collections used by the modifier: the target meshes, the leaf assets and the ivy sources. You normally do not need to change them. Apply and remove Apply (✓) converts the ivy to a mesh. Remove (−) deletes it. The ivy is distributed according to the target surface area. If the target is animated or deformed, the ivy can change from frame to frame.

docs.text: Manage & Proxy The Manage section of the J pie menu gathers scene management tools. Button Action Create Group Group the selected objects. See Group To Instance Group the selection and turn the group into an instance in one step Ungroup , Group to Instance Shown when a group is selected. docs.text: Scattering BagaPie scatters objects on a mesh surface with Geometry Nodes. Each scatter is a layer : a set of assets with its own density, transforms, paint and mask. A surface can hold as many layers as you need. Create a scatter layer Select the objects to scatter (meshes, curves or empties). Select the target surface last , so it is the active object. Press J and choose Scatter . Select the assets, then the ground. J > Scatter creates a new layer. The assets are moved to a collection under BagaPie > BagaPie_Scatter . The first layer adds a BagaPie_Scatter modifier to the surface; each new scatter on the same surface adds a layer to it. The layers appear in the modifier stack at the top of the BagaPie panel. Use Rename Layer to keep them organized. BagaPie sets a starting Distance Min from the size of your assets. From the Asset Browser Next to Scatter , Scatter Paint and Snap Asset , the Asset Browser button uses the assets selected in an open Asset Browser instead of objects in the scene. In the Asset Browser, browse a library (not All ) and select one or more assets. In the viewport, select the surface. Press J and click Asset Browser next to the tool. BagaPie imports the assets and creates the layer. Asset Browser panel The Asset Browser also has a BagaPie Scatter Tools panel in its sidebar (Asset tab). With a mesh selected in the viewport: Scatter Selection creates a layer from the selected assets. Add Assets to layer adds the selected assets to the active layer. The layer list, Rename Layer , Distance Min , Density Max , Scale Min / Max and Random Rot Z give you the essentials without leaving the Asset Browser. The layer content is listed below, with per-asset buttons: select, show as bounds, proxy, remove from layer. Scatter Paint Scatter Paint creates the same layer, then switches the surface to Weight Paint. Assets only appear where you paint. Control Action Paint ! Enter paint mode for the active layer Exit Paint Mode Back to Object Mode Add / Remove Paint or erase Clear Paint Remove all painting from the layer Invert Paint Invert the painted area Brush Profile Softer or sharper brush falloff Vertex Group Each layer paints in its own vertex group; you can add, remove or swap groups Paint resolution depends on the mesh topology. Subdivide the surface if the painted areas look blocky. Main settings Setting Effect Distance Min Minimum space between instances; prevents collisions Density Max Maximum number of points per square meter. Keep it as low as possible for performance % Viewport Display Share of instances shown in the viewport. All instances are rendered Align Normal How much instances follow the surface normal Seed Changes the random distribution When collisions do not matter (grass, for example), set Distance Min to 0 and control the amount with Density Max only. Tools Control Action Add Assets Add assets to the active layer. Source: View 3D uses the selected objects; Source: Asset Browser uses the assets selected in the Asset Browser Remove Assets Remove the selected assets from the active layer. Select the assets, then the surface, choose the layer and click. Works from the 3D view only Camera Culling Assign an existing camera culling to this layer (see Effectors ) Layer Collection The collection that holds the layer's assets Proxy All Add or remove a proxy on every asset of the layer Select All Assets Select the layer's assets Below, each asset of the layer has buttons to select it, display it as bounds (recommended for heavy scenes), toggle its proxy , or remove it from the layer. Transform Position , Rotation , Scale Min and Scale Max set the base transform of the instances. Randomize Transform adds random Position , Rotation and Scale with a min / max per axis. Random rotation on Z is the most common. Mask The texture mask controls where assets appear. Setting Effect Texture Mask Enable the mask Fac Mask strength; 1 uses it fully Scale Size of the pattern Offset Spreads the mask more or less Smooth Softens the mask edges Position Moves the pattern Invert Mask Swap masked and unmasked areas Use the copy and paste buttons to reuse mask settings on another layer. Paste them on a second layer and invert the mask to place, for example, bushes between the rocks. Add a small offset to avoid overlaps. This is a quick way to break repetition. Effectors Point Effector and Camera Culling remove instances near objects or outside the camera view. See Effectors . Safety features Scattering a heavy asset on a large surface can slow Blender down. When you scatter, BagaPie estimates the result: If the estimated polycount (average asset polycount × instance count) exceeds the limit in the preferences, a dialog shows the approximate number of instances and lets you enable Use Proxy and lower Displayed Instances in % . If a camera culling exists, you can enable it too. Assets above the proxy polycount limit get a proxy automatically when Enable proxy by default is on. If the surface scale is not applied, BagaPie offers to Apply Scale . An unapplied scale changes the instance count and can deform instances. All limits are in Preferences > Scattering Preferences : Preference Default Enable proxy by default On Minimum polycount for proxy 100,000 Use security features for scattering On Maximum polycount to trigger security features 10,000,000 Percentage of instances displayed in the viewport 100 Propose to apply the scale of the target On Use Camera Culling if available On Keep assets in scene Off: when on, objects removed from a scatter collection are relinked to the scene collection Save as a preset Save in GeoPack at the bottom of the scatter settings stores all layers of the surface as a reusable preset. See Scatter presets . Apply and remove Apply (✓ in the modifier stack) converts the scatter to real geometry. Remove (−) deletes the layer. Tips The scatter depends on the surface area. If the surface is animated or deformed, the distribution changes over time. If the render differs from the viewport, check that the surface does not change at render time (for example a different Subdivision level), and check % Viewport Display . Textures on the ground make scattering look much more natural.

docs.text: Snap Asset Snap Asset places assets one by one on a surface, where you click. Place assets Select the assets to place. Select the target surface last . Press J and choose Snap Asset (or its Asset Browser button to use assets selected in the Asset Browser). Click on the surface to add instances. Press Esc to stop. Until you press Esc , every click adds an instance. To add more later, click Add Instances in the BagaPie panel. Settings Setting Effect Add Instances Resume placing instances Offset Z Lift or sink the instances along the normal Align Normal Align instances to the surface Random Rotation Random rotation per instance Scale Min / Max Random scale range Target / Instances The surface and the assets used by the modifier Edit the placement Each instance is a vertex of the Snap Asset object. In Edit Mode you can move, delete or duplicate them like any vertex. In the sidebar Item tab, a vertex's Bevel Weight and Vertex Crease drive the rotation and scale of its instance. Visibility and removal work as for other modifiers, from the modifier stack.
